addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- gitnexus-cli: Use when the user needs to run GitNexus CLI commands like analyze/index a repo, check status, clean the index, generate a wiki, or list indexed repos. Examples: "Index this repo", "Reanalyze the codebase", "Generate a wiki"
- gitnexus-debugging: Use when the user is debugging a bug, tracing an error, or asking why something fails. Examples: "Why is X failing?", "Where does this error come from?", "Trace this bug"
- gitnexus-exploring: Use when the user asks how code works, wants to understand architecture, trace execution flows, or explore unfamiliar parts of the codebase. Examples: "How does X work?", "What calls this function?", "Show me the auth flow"
- gitnexus-guide: Use when the user asks about GitNexus itself — available tools, how to query the knowledge graph, MCP resources, graph schema, or workflow reference. Examples: "What GitNexus tools are available?", "How do I use GitNexus?"
- gitnexus-impact-analysis: Use when the user wants to know what will break if they change something, or needs safety analysis before editing code. Examples: "Is it safe to change X?", "What depends on this?", "What will break?"
- gitnexus-pdg-query: Use when querying or extending GitNexus's PDG control/data-dependence surface (the `pdg_query` MCP tool, CDG/REACHING_DEF edges), or reasoning about "what controls X" / "where does Y flow" / guard clauses. Examples: "what guards this statement?", "trace this variable within the function", "why is the pdg_query result empty?", "add a CDG query".
- gitnexus-pr-review: Use when the user wants to review a pull request, understand what a PR changes, assess risk of merging, or check for missing test coverage. Examples: "Review this PR", "What does PR #42 change?", "Is this PR safe to merge?"
- gitnexus-refactoring: Use when the user wants to rename, extract, split, move, or restructure code safely. Examples: "Rename this function", "Extract this into a module", "Refactor this class", "Move this to a separate file"
- gitnexus-taint-analysis: Use when working on, reviewing, or extending GitNexus's CFG/taint/PDG subsystem (the `--pdg` layers), or when reasoning about source→sink data-flow findings. Examples: "How does taint analysis work here?", "Why didn't explain find this flow?", "Add a new sink/source", "Review the interprocedural taint code".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1. Search the codebase for a "Memo" model/type and any fields that look derived/computed (e.g. "property", "payload", "snippet", "preview", "plainText", "wordCount", etc.)
2. Find the specific function/file that computes this derived metadata from memo content.
3. Find what triggers recomputation of this metadata — e.g. is it computed on create, on update, via a background job/service, via a hook/listener?
4. List exactly what properties/fields are extracted (e.g. tags, links, tasks/todos, references to other memos, has-code, has-incomplete-tasks, etc.)

Use grep/glob to search the actual repo source code (not GitNexus docs). Look for terms like "ExtractMemoRelatedMemoIdsAndTaskIds", "MemoProperty", "RebuildMemoProperty", "extract", "regexp" etc. This is likely a Go backend (memos is usermrc/usememos style project) — check the store/db package and any service layer for memo property/payload computation.

Report back: the exact file path(s) and function name(s) where this computation happens, the trigger points (list all call sites with file:line), and the exact list of extracted properties/fields.

## Summary

**Repo location:** `/bench/repo` (usememos/memos, Go backend + React frontend)

### 1. The "Memo" model and its derived-metadata field

`store/memo.go` defines the domain `Memo` struct with a `Payload *storepb.MemoPayload` field. The derived (computed, non-user-set) data lives inside that payload, defined in `proto/store/memo.proto` (generated into `proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go`):

```proto
message MemoPayload {
  Property property = 1;
  Location location = 2;
  repeated string tags = 3;

  // The calculated properties from the memo content.
  message Property {
    bool has_link = 1;
    bool has_task_list = 2;
    bool has_code = 3;
    bool has_incomplete_tasks = 4;
    string title = 5;   // extracted from the first H1 heading, if present
  }
  ...
}
```
So `MemoPayload.Tags` and `MemoPayload.Property.{HasLink, HasTaskList, HasCode, HasIncompleteTasks, Title}` are the persisted derived fields. `MemoPayload.Location` is user-set (not derived) and excluded from recomputation.

There is also a separate, *not persisted*, request-time-only derived value: `Snippet` (plain-text preview), computed fresh on every read for list/detail responses rather than stored.

### 2. Where the derived metadata is computed

**Core extraction (markdown AST walk):** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
- `func (s *service) ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` (line 356) — single-pass walk that populates `Tags`, `Mentions`, and `Property{HasLink, HasCode, HasTaskList, HasIncompleteTasks, Title}`. This is the one used in production for payload rebuilds.
- `func (s *service) ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)` (line 193) — equivalent property-only extractor (older/simpler path, part of the `Service` interface, used in tests).
- `func (s *service) ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)` (line 143) — tags-only extractor.
- `func (s *service) GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` (line 264) — builds the plain-text preview/snippet (NOT stored, computed on demand at read time).

**Assembly into the store payload:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`
- `func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` (line 74) — the single function that mutates `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` from `memo.Content`, by calling `markdownService.ExtractAll(...)`.
- `func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context)` (line 27) — batch job that loads all memos (`store.FindMemo` paginated 100 at a time) and calls `RebuildMemoPayload` + `Store.UpdateMemo` for each — a full-repo re-derivation pass.

### 3. Trigger points (call sites)

- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` — inside `CreateMemo` (line 70): every new memo has its payload rebuilt before `s.Store.CreateMemo(...)`.
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` — inside `UpdateMemo` (line 401), specifically in the `if path == "content"` branch of the field-mask loop: payload is rebuilt only when the memo's content is actually being updated.
- `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52` (inside `RunOnce`) — a bulk/background re-derivation job that iterates every memo in the store and rebuilds its payload. Note: `NewRunner`/`RunOnce` are **not wired into `server.go`'s startup or the scheduler** (`internal/scheduler`) anywhere in the current codebase — they exist as an exported utility (used in tests: `server/runner/memopayload/runner_test.go`) but currently have no active production trigger (e.g., no cron/CLI hookup found), unlike e.g. `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` which server.go does call.

Additionally, `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll(...)` is called independently (not via `RebuildMemoPayload`) in `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` inside `resolveMentionTargets`, to extract `@mention` targets for notification dispatch on create/update/comment (mentions are not currently persisted onto `MemoPayload` — a `docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/` design doc describes adding a `Mentions` field to the payload, but that isn't implemented in the current proto).

Snippet generation (`GenerateSnippet`) is invoked per-request, not on write:
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76` — `getMemoContentSnippet` inside `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` (single-memo response).
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:225,248` — `batchConvertMemoRelations`, for related-memo snippets.
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85` — for outgoing webhook payloads.
- Helper defined at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:82` (`getMemoContentSnippet`).

Consumers of the persisted `Property`/`Tags` fields (for lists/stats, no recomputation):
- `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:48-50` (`convertMemoPropertyFromStore`, line 315) — maps store payload to API response for list/detail views.
- `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:141-151, 257-267` — aggregates `HasLink`/`HasCode`/`HasTaskList`/`HasIncompleteTasks` counts for user stats.

### 4. Exact list of extracted/derived fields

From `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` in `internal/markdown/markdown.go` (walking the goldmark AST once):

- `Tags []string` — all `#tag` nodes found via the custom `TagExtension`/`mast.TagNode` (deduplicated, case-preserved; skips tags nested inside links/images).
- `Mentions []string` — `@username` mention nodes (lower-cased, deduplicated) — used for notification targeting only, not currently persisted to `MemoPayload`.
- `Property.Title string` — text of the first block-level child if it's an H1 heading (`extractHeadingText`).
- `Property.HasLink bool` — set when a `gast.KindLink` node is encountered.
- `Property.HasCode bool` — set when `gast.KindCodeBlock`, `gast.KindFencedCodeBlock`, or `gast.KindCodeSpan` is encountered.
- `Property.HasTaskList bool` — set when a GFM task checkbox (`east.KindTaskCheckBox`) is encountered.
- `Property.HasIncompleteTasks bool` — set (alongside `HasTaskList`) when a task checkbox node has `IsChecked == false`.

Separately, `GenerateSnippet(content, maxLength)` produces a plain-text preview (strips code blocks, joins block text with spaces, expands `#tags` and autolinks, truncates to `maxLength` at a word boundary with `" ..."` suffix) — this is the "preview text" used in list views, always computed on read, never stored in `MemoPayload`.

Not derived from content in this codebase version: `MemoRelation` records (related-memo links) are explicit, user-set via `SetMemoRelations` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`), not auto-extracted from memo content/regex (confirming the older `ExtractMemoRelatedMemoIdsAndTaskIds`-style logic mentioned in the prompt is not present in this version — it has been superseded by the goldmark-based `ExtractAll`/`RebuildMemoPayload` pipeline).</result>
